thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: high p99 latency and repeated container restarts observed for continuous-batcher service in us-east-2. Paging activity spike detected. Auto-sev: P1. Details: 502s of elevated latency; 12x restart rate in last 5m.

oncall-erin: I'm on it. Adding SRE and runtime. tagging @sre-lead-mike @eng-runtime-raj @eng-runtime-amelia

sre-lead-mike: seeing node flaps on nodepool-batcher-1, status=NotReady -> Ready thrash. kube events show OOMKill in batcher process repeatedly.

eng-runtime-raj: logs show CUDA OOMs during large-batch memcpy. stack: LLM inference worker -> continuous-batcher -> cudaMemcpyAsync failing. Also observed long queue growth (queue depth ~ 4800).

eng-runtime-amelia: confirmed. There's a runaway prefix: a tiny fraction of requests are 15k tokens causing KV cache growth and blocking batching loop. Continuous batcher isn't applying backpressure correctly for those sessions.

support-janet: any customer impact? CS has a few calls: @customer-success-luis please gather impacted orgs.

customer-success-luis: flagged 3 customers on dedicated pools reporting timeouts and 5 startups on hosted API saw 5-10x latency. Escalated two enterprise customers; they're actively seeing errors.

oncall-erin: immediate mitigation suggestions? We need fast mitigation that reduces latency for majority traffic.

eng-runtime-raj: propose immediate config flips: 1) enable "drop_longest" policy on continuous-batcher to evict oldest large requests from queues; 2) reduce max_batch_size from 2048->512 for affected pool; 3) route traffic for enterprise pools to cpu-fallback variant. I can push a hotfix hook.

infra-ops: note autoscaler also spiking. We should avoid scale churn; suggest disabling scale-up for affected nodepool for 10m while we stabilize.

oncall-erin: go ahead with 1 & 2. @deploy-bot can you apply the config change to batcher-config/us-east-2 now? Keep rollback ready.

deploy-bot: deploy request received: apply batcher-config patch (drop_policy=drop_longest, max_batch_size=512) to continuous-batcher/us-east-2. Will execute as a canary across 2 pods first.

eng-runtime-amelia: while canary rolls, I'll enable session-level KV limits and a per-session token cap to prevent new long-run sessions from entering queue. Also toggling prefix-cache eviction to aggressive.

deploy-bot: canary update applied to pod-7 and pod-9. Observing metrics...

eng-runtime-raj: early signals: queue depth halved on canary pods, p99 latency down ~60% on canary. No more immediate OOMs in those pods.

oncall-erin: good. Roll to rest of pool gradually. @sre-lead-mike please watch node flaps and let infra know if we need to cordon nodes.

infra-ops: cordoning node node-12 which shows repeated Kubelet restarts. Scheduling drains.

sre-lead-mike: note: some pods entered CrashLoopBackOff with error: "cuda runtime error (2): out of memory". After config rollout restarts are decreasing. We're also seeing heavy paging (swap reads) on a few hosts - kernel logs show "page allocation failure".

eng-runtime-amelia: that aligns with long KV caches causing GPU memory + host pinned memory to spike and cause kernel reclaim. The drop_longest policy prevents backlog growth so that should reduce host memory pressure.

customer-success-luis: I'll notify affected customers that we've applied mitigations and are monitoring. Providing ETA: 15-20m for stabilization; offering to reopen throttles after we verify.

support-janet: posting status to status.redwood.ai and customer-facing Slack channels now.

oncall-erin: timeline: patch rolled to all pods at +3m, queue depth dropped cluster-wide by +6m, p99 returned to baseline ~+9m. Remaining steps: root cause & postmortem. Assigning owners: eng-runtime-amelia to lead root cause; eng-runtime-raj for hotfix PR to add queue caps and session guards; sre-lead-mike to document node-level observability and autopilot thresholds.

eng-runtime-raj: creating hotfix branch: "fix/queue-cap-and-backpressure". Will include unit + e2e for extreme-token sessions and add a circuit that rejects sessions > 8k tokens by default.

eng-runtime-amelia: postmortem will include: 1) reproducer (synthetic workload with 3% ultra-long sessions), 2) metrics alert tuning (trigger earlier on queue slope, not absolute depth), 3) default batcher policy change to favor drop_oldest under memory pressure, and 4) integration test for swap/paging simulation.

sre-lead-mike: decision: lower severity to P2 at +12m as customer errors reduced to transient spikes and no data loss. We'll keep pager on until tomorrow morning.

oncall-erin: thanks everyone. Followups: eng-runtime to post fix PR and coordinate canary for new logic; SRE to confirm node flaps fixed and update runbook; CS to update customers with incident summary. I'll leave the channel open for updates. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, p99 latency recovered to baseline, crash/restart rate normalized. Incident state: monitoring.

support-janet: done: status page updated, customers notified, support queue cleared for related tickets.

customer-success-luis: customers acknowledged. One asked for a postmortem and timeline — will request once complete.

eng-runtime-raj: pushing hotfix PR now. Will request reviews.

oncall-erin: closing slack incident channel in 1h unless new regressions. Great job all.
